title_vi: Bốn mẫu nhất quán cuối cùng: bản đọc đi sau bao lâu, và ai sửa khi một bước hỏng

related.reason_vi: Bản gốc và bản dẫn xuất, câu hỏi bản dẫn xuất cũ được bao lâu.
Sự kiện bù trừ trong event sourcing.
Đọc nhật ký thay đổi để không lỡ sự kiện.

claims.evidence: The Azure Architecture Center Saga, Compensating Transaction and CQRS pages and the PostgreSQL 16 NOTIFY and LISTEN reference pages were read from clones of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center and postgres/postgres; the lag, staleness and saga results were measured by the author, who ran them on PostgreSQL 16.15 with psycopg 3.3.6 on 2026-10-18.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright) rendered lesson.md (markdown-it, tables enabled, every <details> open, a 16 px page gutter) at each width: the page never scrolled sideways and the figure was scaled to the column; the smallest SVG font-size times that scale is the recorded minimum at 320 px. `python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser` measured every line of the figure in Chromium inside its box. Not GitHub, not a real phone and not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: A saga is a sequence of local transactions, each within a single service; if a step fails, compensating transactions undo the changes of completed steps; transactions after the pivot are retryable and idempotent; compensating transactions might not always succeed; there is no built-in isolation across services (lost updates, dirty reads, fuzzy reads).
claims.section: Solution; Problems and considerations; Potential data anomalies in sagas
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: Restoring the original state can overwrite changes from other concurrent instances, so a compensating transaction must account for concurrent work; undo steps need not run in exact reverse order; business rules apply, e.g. cancelling a flight might not entitle the customer to a complete refund.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: When the read and write stores are separated the read data might not show the most recent changes immediately; the read model is eventually consistent with the write model.
claims.verified_by: Read from a clone of MicrosoftDocs/architecture-center at commit 8e2c239344ee753a88856800b4210a3e27ac1036.

claims.claim_vi: NOTIFY events inside a transaction are not delivered until and unless the transaction commits; NOTIFY goes to each client that has executed LISTEN on the channel; LISTEN registrations are cleared when the session ends.
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of postgres/postgres at commit 8e928803020e5b5694cde58e4851fce64ef9d520.

claims.claim_vi: Measured: 200 updates to 20 orders 50 ms apart; a trigger with pg_notify and a LISTEN process applied each change to a read table in another database with median lag 2.3 ms and maximum 23.8 ms, and a read right after each write was stale 194/200 times; a sync job every 2 seconds gave median lag 640 ms and maximum 1.99 s, carried 117 of the 200 versions and was stale 200/200 times; a saga charged 300, failed to reserve stock on a check constraint, then wrote a refund row and set the order to CANCELLED.
claims.verified_by: The author ran and measured this on 2026-10-18 on one machine, both databases in one PostgreSQL 16.15 server.

claims.claim_vi: Four eventual consistency patterns: event-based, background sync (slower because the job runs on a schedule), saga-based (a sequence of local transactions for long-lived transactions) and CQRS-based (separate read and write databases).

design_notes_vi: Bốn thẻ mẫu, bốn bước thử đo khoảng lệch, một sơ đồ tuần tự saga có giao dịch bù, bốn câu hỏi trước khi chọn. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: The source gives each pattern one or two sentences; the lesson measures the lag of event-based and background sync propagation and runs a saga with compensating transactions.
The lesson adds that a scheduled sync skips intermediate versions, measured, and that a compensating transaction adds an opposite action instead of restoring the old state.
editorial_note_vi: Bài mới viết trong kho này, chờ review kỹ thuật. Chưa user testing hoặc phê duyệt phát hành.
